commit it, and report. Read this entire brief, then the repository AGENTS.md
and its relevant routed guidance. Do not stop at a survey or plan. If the issue
and repository genuinely leave a decision open, ask the judge one specific
question and wait for the answer, then continue.

# Working agreement

Your repository is the `bifrost` checkout under /workspace in your own container
(mj 2.10.0 places it at /workspace/<workspace id>/bifrost; `ls /workspace/*/bifrost`
finds it). The judge is Claude Fable.
All competing lanes receive this identical brief. Do not inspect other lanes,
their sessions, the judge's private files, or evaluation results about this issue.
Before investigation, verify your checkout has no tracked or untracked changes,
fetch origin, and check out this exact commit detached: 971393a3af610f82db95fb8e031da15b0c66bf72
The detached checkout is explicitly authorized for this evaluation. Report its
full hash. Do not merge newer master or change the base during your initial run.

Work only in your container. Commit your changes on the detached HEAD, with
real messages. Do not push, create branches or PRs, edit issue labels, or post
GitHub comments. The judge exports your commits. Commit all intended work before
your final report; never stage unrelated files or use git add -A.
Do not write to any memory directory or MEMORY.md: that pool is shared across
sessions and harnesses. Keep discoveries in your report. Do not read other
evaluation sessions or their reports. Do not launch subagents; do the entire
solution in this lane, so every configuration has the same delegation policy.

Use plain cargo and the repository testing guidance. Clear JAVA_HOME and set
BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1 and RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1. Let nextest own concurrency;
pass --max-fail 100. Run relevant crate and integration suites. Changes under a
language's graph code or analysis usages require that language's usage and issue
suites plus cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib.
Run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings and
format changed files. Do not reduce nextest concurrency without measured resource
exhaustion. Report pre-existing failures only after checking the same base.
The harness fails a turn after 10 minutes without activity, so never block on
one command for longer than 5 minutes: run long builds and suites in the
background or with a timeout of at most 300000 ms and poll their output.
Never run shared-cache GC or delete another session's build targets. If disk
pressure requires isolated storage, use the repository's managed target helper.

Fix causes with tree-sitter and analyzer structures, not source-text parsing or
regex fallbacks. Use assertions for construction invariants, iterative traversal
for deep trees, plain ASCII, and the existing shared helpers. Demonstrate a
production-shaped regression failing before and passing after the fix.
Read relevant architecture chapters before changing identities, cache, usage,
dataflow, semantic models or results. Bump the language extraction epoch when
the persisted language facts change; do not bump it for query-only changes.
Use an ExecPlan under .agents/plans only when the repository requires one.

External evidence repositories are not preinstalled: fetch the issue's pinned
commits under /workspace/evidence, outside this checkout. Use a fresh analyzer
cache at /workspace/cache when needed. Validate the actual witnesses and census
coverage, not merely a lower finding count caused by sampling or suppression.

# Reporting

An ordinary end of turn is not completion. When finished, commit your solution
and send a message with FINAL REPORT on its own line within the first five lines,
followed by these six sections:
1. Confirmed cause with structured evidence.
2. Changes and reasons, including full base and final commit hashes.
3. Exact validation commands and results.
4. Before/after evidence on the issue's named repositories or witnesses.
5. git status --short, limitations, and any separately actionable findings.
6. A draft GitHub approach comment, 5 to 12 plain-language sentences.

# Issue

Issue #3631: C++ exact-name lookup does not map the source spelling Top::Only to the canonical nested identity Top$Only

Noted by two lanes while solving #3520 at base 18fa60ee98f92a8dca58ffbd3a5d949adb30ee19, and left out of that ticket's scope.

For `struct Top { struct Only { int b; }; };`, extraction persists the nested type as `[("Top", Type), ("Only", Nested)]`, rendered `Top$Only`. A caller who types the source spelling `Top::Only` gets nothing from `IAnalyzer::definitions`: `parse_symbol_path` splits `::` into two `Unknown` segments, so the exact seek asks parent `Top` / identifier `Only` (which is the stored row), but the final retain compares the request's native rendering against the persisted `Top$Only` and drops it. One lane's kernel probe at the base shows `definitions("Top::Only") = []` beside `definitions("Top$Only.b") = ["Top$Only.b"]`.

This is distinct from closed #2246, which corrected raw `::` in the extracted identity of out-of-line definitions; here the identity is canonical and only the lookup's spelling comparison is at fault. #3520 fixes the `$`-spelled query; the `::`-spelled query for a nested type remains unresolved.
The checkout is clean and detached at `971393a3af610f82db95fb8e031da15b0c66bf72`. Next I’ll read the architecture and testing guidance, then trace the exact-name lookup that drops `Top::Only`.
The nested type is stored as `Top$Only`, while a `Top::Only` query is re-rendered with `.` and then dropped. I’ll add a regression that shows that miss, then fix the lookup.
The regression is confirmed: every `::` query returns nothing, while the canonical `$` and `.` names already resolve. I’ll teach exact-name lookup to ask for those persisted kind patterns.

FINAL REPORT

C++ exact-name lookup now maps a `::` source spelling such as `Top::Only` onto the stored nested identity `Top$Only`. The fix is committed on the detached base.

1. Confirmed cause with structured evidence.

For `struct Top { struct Only { int b; }; };`, extraction stores `[("Top", Type), ("Only", Nested)]`, rendered `Top$Only`. `IAnalyzer::definitions("Top::Only")` goes through `cpp_rendered_name_fq`, which uses `parse_symbol_path`. That splitter does not treat `$` as a separator and records both `::` components as `Unknown`. `Unknown` re-renders with `.`, so the request's native spelling is `Top.Only`. The exact seek still asks parent `Top` / identifier `Only`, which is the stored row, and `unit_matches_requested_name` then compares native spellings and drops `Top$Only`. A second retain, `unit.fq_name() == "Top::Only"`, drops anything that survived. This is query-side only. The persisted identity is already canonical, unlike closed #2246. #3520 fixed the `$` spelling and left the `::` spelling alone.

Before the fix, `cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost --test suite_issues issue_3631` failed both new tests. Every `::` query was empty, including `Top::Only`, `Top::Only::b`, `ns::Outer::Inner`, `ns::Outer::method`, `absl::base::Foo`, and both `AudioSink::AudioDevice_t` plugins. The canonical controls in the same test (`Top$Only`, `Top$Only.b`, `ns.Outer`, `Buck$Stop`, `Top.Only`) already matched and were not in the mismatch list.

2. Changes and reasons, including full base and final commit hashes.

Base: `971393a3af610f82db95fb8e031da15b0c66bf72`. Final: `509d66c8578806862285167440ed0dd57b1133f4`.

`cpp_colon_source_aliases` builds the kind placements extraction actually stores for a `::`-only spelling: leading packages, one type plus nested types, and an optional terminal member. `CppAnalyzer::definitions` asks each of those as an exact-name query. Those names contain no `Unknown` segment, so the store keeps a hit by structural equality instead of native-spelling comparison. Canonical spellings that already contain `.` or `$`, including `Top$Only` and `base::android.ScopedJavaGlobalRef`, stay on the existing single parse. Persisted facts are unchanged, so the C++ extraction epoch is not bumped.

3. Exact validation commands and results.

`JAVA_HOME` was unset. `BIFROST_PARALLELISM=1` and `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1`. Nextest kept its own concurrency. `--max-fail 100` was set.

- Before: `cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost --test suite_issues issue_3631` — 2 failed, as above.
- After: `cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost --test suite_issues -E 'test(/issue_3631/) | test(/issue_3520/)'` — 4 passed.
- `cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-cpp colon_source_aliases` — 1 passed.
- `cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost-analysis --lib definitions_reach_nested` — 1 passed.
- `cargo nextest run --max-fail 100 -p brokk-bifrost --test suite_analyzers -E 'test(/nested_namespace_definition/) | test(/a_reference_resolves_identically/)'` — 2 passed.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` — finished with no warnings. Changed Rust files were formatted with `rustfmt --edition 2024`.

4. Before/after evidence on the issue's named repositories or witnesses.

The issue names no external repository commit. The witnesses are the nested struct and the two-plugin `AudioSink` shape.

Before: `definitions("Top::Only") = []`, `definitions("Top::Only::b") = []`, `definitions("AudioSink::AudioDevice_t") = []`, while `definitions("Top$Only")` and `definitions("Top$Only.b")` already returned those canonical names.

After: `definitions("Top::Only")` is `nested.cpp#Top$Only`, `definitions("Top::Only::b")` is `nested.cpp#Top$Only.b`, and `definitions("AudioSink::AudioDevice_t")` returns both `new_portaudio/main.cpp#AudioSink$AudioDevice_t` and `portaudio/main.cpp#AudioSink$AudioDevice_t`. The same run also resolves `ns::Outer::Inner` to `ns.Outer$Inner`, `ns::Outer::method` to `ns.Outer.method`, and `absl::base::Foo` to `absl::base.Foo`. `definitions("Top.Only")` stays empty, so a dot spelling does not become the nested-class identity.

5. git status --short, limitations, and any separately actionable findings.

`git status --short` is empty. The work is one commit on detached HEAD and was not pushed.

`AnalyzerDefinitionLookup::fqn` still compares the rendered string with the canonical name, so an internal canonical lookup is unchanged. Source `::` queries go through `IAnalyzer::definitions`. A `::`-only query returns every stored kind placement with those segment texts, so a namespace `Top::Only` and a nested class `Top$Only` both come back when both exist. Spellings that already mix `::` with `.` or `$` are not reinterpreted.

6. A draft GitHub approach comment, 5 to 12 plain-language sentences.

`definitions("Top::Only")` was empty even though the nested struct was indexed as `Top$Only`. The lookup split `Top::Only` into two untyped name pieces, and those pieces print back as `Top.Only`. The search did find the nested type under parent `Top` and name `Only`, then threw it away because `Top.Only` is not `Top$Only`. The `$` spelling fixed in #3520 was already working. This change teaches a `::`-only query to also ask for the namespace, nested-type, and member shapes C++ extraction stores. `definitions("Top::Only")` now returns `Top$Only`, and `definitions("Top::Only::b")` returns `Top$Only.b`. The same path covers `ns::Outer::Inner` and `ns::Outer::method`. Names that are already written with `.` or `$`, including `Top$Only` and `base::android.ScopedJavaGlobalRef`, keep their previous answers. Nothing stored in the index changed, so the C++ extraction epoch is the same.

 `::`-only spelling now also asks for the namespace, nested-type and member forms that C++ extraction stores. A row is kept only when its full structured name matches one of those forms. The C++ provider gives those forms to the shared lookup, so `definitions`, the lookup's `fqn`, its batched prefetches and `get_symbol_locations` all give the same answers, and the shared code has no C++ branch. Stored names and renderings do not change, so the C++ extraction epoch stays the same. Tests show that `Top::Only`, `Top::Mid::Only`, `Top::Only::b` and `ns::Outer::Inner` resolve to `Top$Only`, `Top$Mid$Only`, `Top$Only.b` and `ns.Outer$Inner`. When a namespace and a class share a spelling, both rows come back, and `Buck::Halt`, `Other::Only` and `Top::Missing` return nothing. Spellings that mix `::` with `.` or `$` are not reinterpreted, and a row with a kind chain outside the listed forms is not found this way. A `::` request asks up to about 2n extra exact questions for n segments. `Top::Only::run` also returns an out-of-line body stored under a second identity, and the canonical spellings `Dollar$Buck$Stop` and `storages::postgres.Portal$Impl` still return nothing, as before; those are separate defects.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The #3520 hook `forward_rendered_name` returns one name, and the shared lookup keeps a row by comparing its rendering with the request string. That comparison can never match a spelling that uses different separators, which is why correction 2 added a second hook that supplies structured names instead of changing how requests are parsed.
- Putting the extra names in the same `query_values` batch keeps the existing memo and prefetch store-read tests valid: the number of round trips stays the same, and only the number of questions per round grows.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
